ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An object placed on a horizontal ground has a mass of 5 kg, and the kinetic friction coefficient between the object and the ground is 0.2. After being subjected to a horizontal pulling force of 15 N, it starts moving from rest ($g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$).

1. The magnitude of the acceleration of an object's motion.
2. The displacement magnitude of the object after 5s
3. At the end of 5 seconds, the external force is removed. How much farther can the object move?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: An object placed on a horizontal ground has a mass of 5 kg, and the kinetic friction coefficient between the object and the ground is 0.2. After being subjected to a horizontal pulling force of 15 N, it starts moving from rest ($g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$). 1. The magnitude of the acceleration of an object's motion. 2. The displacement magnitude of the object after 5 s. 3. At the end of 5 seconds, the external force is removed. How much farther can the object move?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Given m=5 kg, μ_k=0.2, g=10 m/s^2, horizontal pulling force F=15 N, and the object starts from rest. On horizontal ground, the normal force is N=mg=5×10=50 N. The kinetic friction force is f_k=μ_k N=0.2×50=10 N. While the pulling force acts, the net horizontal force is F_net=15−10=5 N, so the acceleration is a=F_net/m=5/5=1 m/s^2. Starting from rest for t=5 s, the displacement is s=(1/2)at^2=(1/2)×1×5^2=12.5 m. The speed at 5 s is v=at=1×5=5 m/s. After the pulling force is removed, only friction acts horizontally, giving a deceleration of a_f=f_k/m=10/5=2 m/s^2. The additional stopping distance is found from 0=v^2−2a_f s, so s=v^2/(2a_f)=25/(2×2)=25/4=6.25 m.
